memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If you see your fellow Israelite's ox or sheep straying, do not ignore it but be sure to take it back to its owner. If they do not live near you or if you do not know who owns it, take it home with you and keep it until they come looking for it. Then give it back. - Deut 22:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God begins this section with a simple, practical command about a wandering animal. If you see your neighbour's ox or sheep straying, you must not pretend you did not notice. You are to bring it back, or if the owner is far off or unknown, care for it until they come. God will not allow His people to shrug and walk away from a neighbour's loss.

Notice the little phrase, "do not ignore it." How easy it is to look the other way, to tell ourselves it is not our problem. But God calls His people to active love that takes responsibility for a neighbour's wellbeing, even in small, inconvenient ways. Caring for someone's stray animal cost time and effort, yet God expected it as a matter of course.

This is love in the ordinary details of life. Jesus taught that loving our neighbour is central to God's law, and He showed that our "neighbour" is anyone whose need we encounter (Luke 10:36-37). We honour God not only in grand acts but in these small, daily choices to help rather than ignore. Is there a "straying ox" in your world right now, a neighbour's need you have been quietly stepping around? God invites you into the joy of active, practical love. Where might you stop looking the other way this week?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you been tempted to "look the other way"?
2. What small, practical act of love could you offer someone this week?
3. How does Jesus reshape who your "neighbour" is?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, open my eyes to the needs around me and give me a heart that helps rather than ignores. Make me a neighbour who truly loves. Amen.
